h1: The 7 Best Backpack Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Backpack Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best backpack leaf blowers for 2026, from commercial Echo units to budget gas models, with CFM figures and who each suits.
summary: The Echo X Series is the most capable backpack blower here, with 1110 CFM and 220 MPH from a 79.9cc engine. Crews who want a proven commercial frame should look at the Echo PB-770T, while most homeowners will be happiest with the Husqvarna 150BT at about half the price. On a tight budget, the PROYAMA and HASANEN post big airflow numbers for very little, with the caveat of unproven brands.
intro: CFM gets all the attention on backpack blower listings, but the number that really shapes your Saturday is how the machine sits on your shoulders for an hour. A huge airflow figure is no use if the frame digs into your back, the engine fights every pull of the cord, or nobody near you can service it when a carburetor gums up.

So this ranking weighs airflow against everything that surrounds it. We reviewed seven gas backpack blowers, from an 80cc pro machine down to a 52cc entry unit, and scored each on the Primea framework. Listed CFM and air speed carried the most weight, followed by engine size, brand support and dealer reach, and what each price bucket actually delivers per dollar.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: The highest airflow here, at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH.
products.description:
Echo's X Series backpack is the heavyweight of this ranking. A 79.9cc two-stroke engine pushes a listed 1110 CFM at 220 MPH, which is the most air and the second fastest stream of any blower we reviewed here. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

It takes first place because nothing else comes close on volume. The Echo PB-770T beside it is a commercial machine too, but it lists 756 CFM, so the X Series clears the same lawn in noticeably fewer passes. The cost is weight on your back and the top price bucket, both real considerations for occasional users.

Buy it if you clear an acre or more, maintain multiple properties, or deal with heavy autumn drifts. For a quarter-acre lot it is far more machine than you need, and the Husqvarna 150BT is the smarter spend.

products.name: PB-770T - Echo Backpack Blower - Commercial Grade 63.3 cc
products.description:
The PB-770T is Echo's commercial-grade workhorse, built around a 63.3cc engine and rated at 756 CFM. Like the X Series it lands in the $500+ bucket, and it is aimed squarely at landscaping crews who run a blower every working day.

It ranks second because its airflow trails the X Series by a wide margin at a similar price. What keeps it above the Husqvarna 150BT is the commercial build grade and the depth of Echo's dealer network, which matters when a machine is earning money and downtime costs you.

Choose it if you run a crew or want a smaller-engine Echo that is designed for daily professional duty. If you are a homeowner who blows leaves a dozen times a year, the 150BT gives you more listed CFM for roughly half the spend.
products.skipIf: You are a homeowner on a budget.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 765 CFM blower in the $200-500 bucket.
products.description:
Husqvarna's 150BT is the backpack blower we would point most homeowners toward. It lists 765 CFM in a gas backpack format, and it sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, well below the two Echo machines.

It ranks third because it delivers airflow on par with the commercial PB-770T for about half the price, from a brand with a wide service network. It trails both Echos on build grade and, against the X Series, on raw volume. The listing is also thinner on detail than Echo's, which cost it a point or two on usability.

Buy it if you have a large suburban lot with plenty of trees and want a proven brand without paying pro prices. Skip it if you need the maximum air volume available, where the X Series is the only answer here.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 880 CFM from a 72cc engine at a low bucket.
products.description:
The PROYAMA is the value surprise in this lineup. Its 72cc gas engine is rated at 880 CFM, higher than both the Husqvarna 150BT and the PB-770T, and it sells in the $100 to $200 bucket.

So why only fourth? Because airflow is just one part of the score. PROYAMA has far less track record than Echo or Husqvarna, and support, parts and dealer service are much harder to count on. A blower that cannot be repaired locally after its second season costs more than its price tag suggests.

Buy it if you want big airflow for little money and are comfortable doing basic maintenance yourself. Skip it if you want a local dealer who can fix it, in which case the Husqvarna 150BT is worth the jump in price.

products.name: HASANEN Backpack Gas Powered Leaf Blower
products.description:
HASANEN's backpack blower lists 850 CFM, which is a striking number for the $50 to $100 bucket, the cheapest in this ranking. It runs on gas and carries the load on a backpack frame like everything else here.

It sits fifth because that airflow claim comes with almost nothing else to back it up. The listing gives few details beyond CFM, and the brand has no long-term reputation for durability. Against the PROYAMA just above, it costs less but offers even less information about engine size and build.

Buy it if you clear leaves a few times a year and want the most listed air for the least cash. Skip it if you blow every week through autumn, because a cheap gas engine worked that hard is where unknown brands tend to fall short.

products.name: HTK Backpack Blower
products.description:
The HTK is a middle-of-the-road gas backpack rated at 665 CFM. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket, the same price range as the PROYAMA.

That shared bracket explains its rank. The PROYAMA lists 880 CFM for similar money, so the HTK gives up more than 200 CFM without a clear advantage in brand support or listed features to compensate. It is still a real step up from a handheld for anyone with a medium yard, but it is hard to recommend over its closest rival.

Buy it if the PROYAMA is out of stock or you find the HTK at a lower price on the day. For a large lot with heavy leaf fall, look higher up this list, since 665 CFM will mean more passes and a longer afternoon.

products.name: Thalorus 52cc Backpack Leaf Blower - Gas Powered 550 CFM 230 MPH High
products.verdict: The lowest airflow here, at 550 CFM from 52cc.
products.description:
The Thalorus is our entry-level backpack pick. Its 52cc engine moves a listed 550 CFM, the lowest volume here, but it claims 230 MPH air speed, the highest figure in this group, and it lands in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks last because volume is what moves piles, and 550 CFM is well behind everything above it. That high air speed is not useless, though. A fast, narrow stream is good at lifting wet, matted leaves out of beds and off pavement, where volume alone struggles.

Buy it if you have a small to medium yard, lots of hardscape or damp leaves, and want the benefits of a backpack frame without a big engine. Skip it for large properties, where the Husqvarna 150BT will save you real time.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air the blower moves each minute, while MPH is how fast that air leaves the tube. Volume pushes big piles across a lawn; speed peels wet, stuck leaves off pavement. A blower strong on one and weak on the other only does half the job. Read both figures on the listing, and be suspicious when only one is given.

Engine displacement, listed in cc, is the best quick proxy for sustained power. Backpack blowers here range from 52cc to 79.9cc. A bigger engine holds airflow better through long sessions but adds weight to your back and burns more fuel. Find the cc figure in the title or spec table, and match it to your property size rather than buying the biggest available.

You may wear this machine for an hour at a time, so the harness matters as much as the engine. Padded shoulder straps, a hip belt and a back pad that keeps engine heat and vibration off you all reduce fatigue. Look closely at the product photos for padding and adjustment points, since listings rarely describe the frame in words.

Gas blowers need occasional carburetor, filter and spark plug work, and a local dealer makes that easy. Echo and Husqvarna both have wide service networks, while value brands like PROYAMA, HASANEN and HTK rely on mail-in support. Search the brand's dealer locator before buying. If none is within driving distance, budget for doing basic repairs yourself.

Gas backpack blowers are loud, and many towns restrict their use by hour, season or noise level. Some areas have banned two-stroke blowers entirely. Before you buy, check your local ordinance and any homeowners association rules. If restrictions apply, a high-voltage battery blower may be the only practical choice, whatever the airflow figures say.

faq.a: For clearing big piles across open lawn, yes. Volume is what moves leaves. For wet leaves or debris stuck in gravel and beds, air speed matters too. The Echo X Series is strong on both, while the Thalorus trades volume for a fast 230 MPH stream.

Yes. Every two-stroke blower here, including the Echo X Series and Husqvarna 150BT, needs oil mixed into the gasoline at the ratio printed in its manual. Pre-mixed canned fuel costs more but avoids mistakes and keeps the carburetor cleaner during off-season storage.

Not everywhere. Many cities and homeowner associations limit gas blowers by time of day, season or noise level, and some have banned two-stroke models outright. Check your local rules before spending $500+ on an Echo, because a battery blower may be your only legal option.

Most listings here do not state a weight, so compare engine size instead. The 79.9cc Echo X Series will be heavier on your back than the 52cc Thalorus. A padded harness and hip belt make more difference to fatigue than a pound or two either way.

faq.q: How often should I service it?
faq.a: Each season, clean or replace the air filter, check the spark plug and run the tank dry before winter storage. Brand-name machines like the Husqvarna 150BT and Echo PB-770T are easier to keep running because dealers stock the parts you will eventually need.

faq.q: Is a backpack blower worth it over handheld?
faq.a: For larger properties, yes. A backpack frame puts the weight on your shoulders and hips instead of one arm, so you can work far longer. The Husqvarna 150BT is a good first backpack. For a small yard or a patio, a handheld is lighter and simpler.

finalTake: If you clear serious acreage, the Echo X Series is the backpack to own, with more airflow than anything else here. For most homeowners with a big, leafy lot, the Husqvarna 150BT is the sweet spot of power, brand support and price. Crews who need a commercial Echo should look at the PB-770T, and buyers on a tight budget can take a calculated chance on the PROYAMA's 880 CFM.
